title: How do I best archive then remove an email account?
creator: spage63
content:
I successfully switched a family member to a new email provider. In Account Settings I moved the old IMAP email account lower, changed Account Name to "name@example.com OLD DO NOT USE", and colored its envelope red.

After a few days when I right click the old email account "name@example.com OLD DO NOT USE" and choose Get Messages, nothing happens and menu Tools > Activity Manager shows errors. I went to the old email provider's webmail interface and verified it's not getting any new emails. So in its Account Settings > Server Settings I unchecked "Check for new message at startup and "Check for new messages every X minutes".

After some cleanup its Inbox, Drafts, Spam IMAP folders are empty apart from a large "Sent" folder, but they still show up in Thunderbird's left pane.

So I think it's time to save the old email account's Sent messages in Local Folders and then delete the account.

I can't right-click to move or copy the Sent folder to Local Folders. So I guess I should create a new Local Folder "Old emails sent from example.com", then select all Sent messages, and move them to Local Folders > Old emails sent from example.com.

Then, to delete the account, do I just click the red [ Delete] button? BTW, the 9-year-old question here "How do I delete an email account in Thunderbird Mail?" is high in search results, but it is out-of-date and incorrect; it says 'Click the "Account Actions" button on the bottom left and choose, "Remove Account".' and that doesn't exist.

There should be a proper Mozilla Support answer that says how to first archive and them remove an email account. I think what I've written here is close but I welcome any suggestions and improvements.

title: Adding a calendar invite fails with "Processing message failed. Status: 80004005"
creator: mozilla869
content:
I'm reporting a recurring issue with Thunderbird's calendar integration. When I attempt to accept a meeting invitation received by email, Thunderbird displays the following error:

"Processing message failed. Status: 80004005."

The event is not added to my calendar.

The latest occurrence involves a Microsoft Teams meeting invitation sent by a Teams user. This is not an isolated incident. I previously experienced the same problem with another meeting invitation, and the error was reproducible.

My configuration:

Thunderbird with a Google Workspace account configured for both Gmail and Google Calendar.

Calendar connected using Thunderbird's native CalDAV integration, automatically configured when the email account was added.

CalDAV server: apidata.googleusercontent.com

No third-party calendar add-on.

Previous troubleshooting:

I confirmed that I can create events directly in Thunderbird and that they synchronize successfully with the Google Calendar web interface. This indicates that the calendar connection and write permissions are functioning normally.

During the previous failure, Thunderbird's Error Console reported:

calendar: CalDAV: Unexpected status adding item: 400

calendar: iTIP processing failed: "Server Replied with 400" nsresult: "0x80004005 (NS_ERROR_FAILURE)"

The previous invitation contained Microsoft-specific iCalendar properties, including X-MICROSOFT-CDO-*.

Current issue:

The same error has now occurred with another invitation, specifically for a Microsoft Teams meeting. Thunderbird displays the Accept, Tentative, and Decline options, but accepting the invitation fails.

It appears that Thunderbird's handling of Microsoft-generated calendar invitations is incompatible with Google Calendar's CalDAV implementation in certain circumstances.

This is particularly problematic because Thunderbird is my primary email and calendar application, and I regularly receive meeting invitations from people using Microsoft Teams and Outlook.

Having to use the Google Calendar web interface to accept invitation defeats the purpose of the integration.

Thank you.
